lesson.title: Building Lists with Loops
lesson.driving_question: How can repeated input build a collection whose size is fixed or user-controlled?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Collecting repeated input into a list with count and condition control
lesson.concept_budget: Compose already-taught append() with both loop families; no new collection syntax is introduced.
misconceptions: The empty list is created before input is collected.
append() belongs inside the loop body.
A for loop suits a known item count.
A while loop suits continuation controlled by an answer.
lesson.progression_note: Integrates all required 1D-list operations before the Grade 7 recap-style capstone.
code_expectations: final traversal or labelled list output

shared_program.filename: Building Lists with Loops - Starter Code.py
shared_program.code:
notes = []
for count in range(3):
    note = input("Enter a note: ")
    notes.append(note)
print("Saved notes:")
for note in notes:
    print(note)

primm.prompt: Recall why append() belongs in a repeated block and when a for loop is appropriate.
Use map, water and torch. Trace notes after each append and predict the final four output lines.
Run with the three supplied notes. Confirm the collection order matches the input order.

questions: Why must the empty list be created before the input loop begins?
What happens if append() is placed after the loop instead of inside it?
Why does range(3) make the program ask for exactly three notes?
Why does the second for loop use note to display each saved value rather than using count?

primm.prompt: Collect exactly five notes instead of three. The program must display all five in their original input order.
Replace the fixed input loop with a condition-controlled loop. Keep asking for a note until stop is entered; do not append or display the sentinel stop.

Create a team roster builder. Ask how many names will be entered, collect exactly that many names into an empty list, then ask for one valid replacement position and update that name before displaying the final roster one name per line.
Move append() into the input loop and traverse the completed list after collection.

programs.challenge2:
notes = []
note = input("Enter a note, or stop: ")
while note != "stop":
    notes.append(note)
    note = input("Enter a note, or stop: ")
print("Saved notes:")
for saved_note in notes:
    print(saved_note)
programs.challenge3:
roster = []
team_size = int(input("Number of names: "))
for count in range(team_size):
    name = input("Name: ")
    roster.append(name)
position = int(input("Valid replacement position: "))
replacement = input("Replacement name: ")
roster[position] = replacement
print("Final roster:")
for name in roster:
    print(name)
